images.caption: A 4-6-0 camelback locomotive built by the Baltimore & Ohio Railroad in 1873.  Photographed at the Museum of Transportation in St. Louis, Missouri.  This image is a composite of three photos taken in a series vertically in order to cover the whole machine in the cramped area of the shed where this loocmotive is housed.  The result is severe barrel distortion from the extremely short effective focal length produced by the process.  The original images were resized with ImageMagick and processed with hugin to create the composite, which was cropped with GIMP, which created the final jpeg file.  No other processing or modifications were done to produce this image.
images.alt: A 4-6-0 camelback locomotive built by the Baltimore & Ohio Railroad in 1873.  Photographed at the Museum of Transportation in St. Louis, Missouri. images.filename: Burlington Zephyr dining car Museum of Transportation St. Louis.jpg
images.caption:
This Burlington Zephyr dining car Silver Spoon belongs to the National Museum of Transport in St. Louis.  It was part a later vintage of Zephyr trains, which had more conventional cars.  The original Burlington Zephyrs from the mid/late 1939s were fixed trainsets with a set of wheels joining each pair of cars, rather than each car having two sets of wheels. The Budd Company built this dining car in 1938; it seated 48 and was numbered as CB&Q #192.

The cars in the background were from other railroads, and would not have been part of a Zephyr.  The second might be Baltimore & Ohio.

images.caption: Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific RR EMD 11-car (including one power car) "Aerotrain" showing the 1,200 hp Bo-A power car of "Aerotrain No.3" at the National Museum of Transport, St Louis, 8/70. 55 cars in 5 sets were built in 1955 for the Pensyvania RR, New York Central, Milwaukee and Union Pacific but  all were withdrawn by 1058 except two units which were sold to the C.R.I.&P. R.R. but which were themselves withdrawn in 1965. They were spectacular looking but failures owing to technical deficiencies and servicing difficulties whilst the passenger accomodation was very cramped, as I found when I entered a car.
